company.name: Ezana AI
company.tagline: The ontology engine for regulated enterprise workflows.

hero.title: Automate the work that has to survive an audit.
hero.description: Ezana AI deploys an ontology of your business — its entities, documents, rules and decisions — then runs your workflows on top of it. The model proposes. Named, authorised commands dispose. Every action lands in an append-only record you can hand to a regulator.
notes: Runs in your cloud or VPC

principles.title: Four things we refuse to ship without.

items.label: Commands
items.title: Every state change is named
items.description: No model, integration or admin screen writes to your data directly. Mutations go through commands that authorise, validate, record and emit.

items.label: Audit
items.title: The log is append-only
items.description: Rows refuse updates and deletes. Logins, refusals and every command land in one immutable trail with actor, target and payload.

items.label: Judgement
items.title: AI proposes, people dispose
items.description: Models read freely and propose. A person or a stated policy accepts. Nothing a model suggests reaches your systems unreviewed.

items.label: Isolation
items.title: Separation is structural
items.description: Scoping lives in the data layer, not in a query somebody remembered to write. Cross-boundary writes are refused rather than reported.

platform.title: An engine, not a chatbot.
platform.description: Large enterprises do not have a text-generation problem. They have workflows that span twelve systems, answer to three regulators and cannot be explained after the fact. Ezana AI is built for those.

items.title: Ontology, first-class
items.description: Applicants, facilities, instruments, limits, documents, findings: modelled as typed objects with explicit relationships, so a workflow reasons over your business rather than over free text.

items.title: Commands and authorisation
items.description: Every mutation is a named command with a typed payload, an authorisation rule and a role. Views, workers, admin actions and AI tools all go through the same door.

items.title: Controls as code
items.description: Policy runs one deterministic check at a time, per object and per document type. Each failure becomes a finding with its evidence attached — never a model's opinion.

items.title: Traced model calls
items.description: A single adapter is the only route to a model. Every call records purpose, model, token counts, latency and outcome, and stores a hash of the prompt rather than the prompt itself.

items.title: Lineage end to end
items.description: From the file that arrived to the figure in the report: every value carries what it came from, who accepted it and what has changed it since.

items.title: Runs where your data lives
items.description: One deployable — API, workers, storage and model adapter — inside your cloud or VPC. Change model provider without touching a workflow.

pipeline.title: Five stages, every one of them reviewable.
pipeline.description: The same shape whether the object is a credit file or a trading book.

steps.title: Model
steps.description: We build the ontology with your team: the objects, their relationships, the rules that already govern them, and the decisions they feed.

steps.title: Ingest
steps.description: Documents, feeds and system records land in storage and are processed asynchronously. A request never waits on a model or a third-party website.

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: Deterministic checks and external registry lookups run against each object. Discrepancies surface as findings, each carrying its evidence — a page, a screenshot, a mismatched field.

steps.title: Capture
steps.description: The model extracts structured facts against a schema. Your operator reviews and corrects them. The corrected set — not the model output — is what the workflow uses.

steps.title: Decide
steps.description: Analysis runs in code; the model writes the narrative around it. The result is a document, a decision record and a trail nobody can quietly edit.

caseStudies.title: Two deployments, one kernel.
caseStudies.description: Different industries, different objects, the same guarantees. The products share tenancy, identity, audit, commands and the model adapter — and nothing else, by contract.

items.name: Ezana Credit
items.title: Credit appraisal, from document dump to defensible decision
items.summary: A lending operation where every facility began life as a folder of scans, and every credit committee question turned into archaeology.
items.context: Officers were assembling appraisals by hand: scanned certificates of incorporation, tax clearances, bank statements, valuations and board resolutions, re-typed into spreadsheets. The company registry was checked in a browser tab and filed as a screenshot. The resulting appraisal had numbers nobody could trace back to a page.
deployed: An ontology of the lending file — applicant, case, document checklist, raw parse, captured fact, finding, appraisal — with the tenant boundary enforced by the model layer itself.
Asynchronous document processing: upload to object storage, parse on workers, and a raw parse the officer watches land.
A checks module per document type rather than a rule engine, plus a registry robot that queries the corporate registry and keeps the screenshot as evidence on the finding.
Extraction against one schema per document type, proposed by the model and reviewed field by field by the officer who signs for it.
A deterministic appraisal: ratios and gradings computed in code, narrative written by the model around them, the whole thing finalised as a PDF.
Officer, approver and admin roles; session auth with CSRF on every state-changing call; an append-only event log underneath all of it.
outcome: An appraisal that cites its sources: every figure traces to a document, a page and the person who accepted it.
Registry verification runs as a job with its evidence attached, instead of living in a screenshots folder.
Officers spend their day on the findings that need judgement rather than on re-typing bank statements.
Architectural boundaries enforced on every push, so the appraisal module can be replaced or extracted without unpicking the platform.

items.name: Ezana Risk
items.title: Perpetual risk analysis across a book that never stops moving
items.summary: A proprietary trading firm running risk on a morning pack, an end-of-day pack, and a spreadsheet somebody trusted.
items.context: Between the packs, exposure moved. Nobody could say precisely when a mandate was first breached, who had seen it, or on what basis a limit had been raised the previous quarter. The numbers were not wrong so much as unaccountable: correct at 07:00 and unverifiable by 14:00.
deployed: A second product on the same kernel — instruments, books, strategies, desks, counterparties, mandates and limits as first-class objects, held apart from the lending product by an enforced independence contract.
Continuous evaluation in place of a daily batch: positions and marks stream in, and every limit, concentration and liquidity rule re-runs as they arrive.
Breaches as findings rather than alerts. Each one carries the inputs that produced it, the threshold it crossed, the instant it crossed, and the state of the book at that instant.
Model-written commentary over deterministic numbers: what moved, what is now correlated with what, which scenarios bite. The calculation itself never leaves code.
Limit changes and breach waivers as commands under four-eyes approval, so every raised limit has an author, an approver, a reason and a timestamp.
A replayable record: any risk figure on any screen can be reconstructed from the events that produced it.
outcome: Risk committee questions answered from the record rather than from memory.
Mandate breaches timestamped to the moment they happened, not to the close.
Every limit in the firm carries a documented author, approver and rationale.
New instrument classes arrive as objects and checks instead of as another spreadsheet.

assurance.title: Built for the people who have to sign it off.
assurance.description: Automation fails enterprise review for the same reasons every time: nobody can reproduce the decision, nobody owns the threshold, and the model's reasoning is the only record. We start from the opposite end.

columns.title: Risk
items: Controls run as code, versioned with the workflow
Every threshold has an author and an approval
Breaches carry their inputs, not just a message

columns.title: Compliance
items: Append-only log of logins, refusals and every command
Four-eyes approval available on any command
Evidence attached at the moment a finding is raised

columns.title: Internal audit
items: Lineage from source document to reported figure
Same inputs, same output — reproducible on demand
Model calls logged with purpose, tokens and latency

columns.title: Security & IT
items: One deployable inside your cloud or VPC
Prompt contents hashed rather than retained
Role-based access with isolation in the data layer
Generated API contract, so no types drift

cta.title: Bring us the workflow nobody trusts to automate.
cta.description: If it needs an audit trail, a second signature and an answer to “why”, it is the kind of work we deploy. Describe it and we will come back with an ontology sketch and a deployment plan.
